paperTitle: LABORAL: A Transformational Game for Preventing Occupational Diseases via Leap Motion Hand Gesture Recognition
centralContribution: This work presents LABORAL, a transformational game developed in Unity using the Leap Motion sensor, designed to educate and train individuals, particularly computer users, in hand and wrist stretching exercises through gestural interactions to prevent occupational diseases like LER (Lesão por Esforço Repetitivo) and DORT (Distúrbio Osteomuscular Relacionado ao Trabalho). The game utilizes a sequence of 17 physiotherapist-defined hand poses, requiring players to sustain correct postures for 10 seconds via real-time gesture recognition, offering an engaging approach to upper limb health education and behavioral transformation.

gameObjects.conceptualOrigin: Paper Abstract
gameObjects.visualMetaphor: The widespread informatization of workplaces leads individuals, especially IT professionals, to spend long periods performing repetitive computer movements, causing pain and impacting performance. This sedentary workload is a primary cause of occupational diseases such as LER (Repetitive Strain Injury) and DORT (Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorder), which affect muscles, tendons, nerves, and ligaments, primarily in the upper limbs. While labor gymnastics is a proven preventive strategy, traditional methods often lack engagement. Gesture recognition sensors, like Leap Motion, are promising but face challenges in continuous, precise gesture identification, necessitating robust and engaging interactive applications for prevention.
